purpose: Reconciled source purposes: [1] Define IdentityCore as the canonical owner of stable person and organization identities, independent from credentials, profile presentation, MeritCore history and runtime sessions. [2] Define the stable canonical person/organization identity used by PortfolioCore, MeritCore, Project participation and FreeMarket, separate from IAM login/session identities.

value.authority_rule: Identity existence does not grant AccessCore rights.
value.credential_rule: Username/password/2FA/key/session identifiers authenticate an identity but never define it.
value.iam_rule: IdentityCore identity is separate from IAM authentication account/session identity, though explicit mappings may exist.
value.identity_rule: Reconciled source clauses: [1] Every IdentityCore subject has an explicit stable canonical identity. [2] Each canonical person or organization has one explicit IdentityCore identity.
value.kind_rule: Identity kind such as person or organization is explicit.
value.merge_rule: Distinct identities do not merge merit/portfolio histories by implication.
value.merit_rule: MeritCore history references the identity but remains a separate owned semantic domain.
value.portfolio_rule: PortfolioCore references the identity and owns evidence/profile-history semantics separately.
value.profile_rule: Names, titles, descriptions and profile fields are descriptive data bound to the identity.
value.registration_rule: Canonical registration timestamp/date is explicit and stable.
value.session_rule: Runtime session identity is transient and never replaces IdentityCore identity.

profile name used as sole identity

two identities merged by same display name

invariants.rule: IdentityCore owns stable person/organization identity and explicit identity relations; credentials, profiles, merits and authorization remain separate semantic layers.

Identity, portfolio, merit, recommendation, trust and competence states derive only from explicit provenance-bearing evidence; display text, self-authored claims, ranking position or AI inference never become verified evidence by themselves.

Distinct canonical identities maintain independent evidence histories; merit, Tier, trust and recommendation histories are not mergeable across identities unless a future explicit canonical identity-merger contract exists.
